data.name: Zenobia
data.long_meaning: From the Greek name 'Zenobia', meaning 'Ruler of the Romans'. In history, Zenobia was a notable queen of the ancient city of Palmyra, in modern-day Syria. She ruled the Roman Empire as a regent from 268 to 270 AD, before being captured by the Roman emperor Aurelian.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of female strength and leadership

in_hebrew.name: זנוביה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם זנוביה מקורו בשפה היוונית ופירושו מתנה מאלוהים. הוא מורכב מהמילים 'זנוס' שפירושו מתנה ו'ביוס' שפירושו חיים. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב הנוצרים והוא מייצג את היופי והכישורים שמוענקים לאדם מאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ζενοβία
in_greek.meaning: δώρο από τους θεούς, όμορφη και ικανή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ζενοβία προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει δωρο από τους θεούς. Είναι σύνθετο από τις λέξεις 'ζένος' που σημαίνει δωρο και 'βίος' που σημαίνει ζωή. Το όνομα χρησιμοποιείται από τους Χριστιανούς και αντιπροσωπεύει την ομορφιά και τις ικανότητες που χαρίζονται στον άνθρωπο από τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Zenobia
in_latin.meaning: gift from God, beautiful and capable
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Zenobia originates from the Greek language and means gift from God. It is derived from the words 'zenos' meaning gift and 'bios' meaning life. The name was adopted by Christians and represents the beauty and abilities bestowed upon a person by God.

data.cultural_impact: Zenobia's reign was a critical period in the history of the Roman Empire. She expanded its territory and asserted her authority over the Eastern provinces, challenging the Roman emperor's dominant rule. Her name became synonymous with female power and independence, inspiring future rulers such as Boudicca in Britain and Cleopatra in Egypt.
data.spiritual_significance: Christianity was still a growing faith during Zenobia's time. The importance of women in the religious context of the ancient world is evident from the numerous goddesses that were worshipped. Hence, the name Zenobia, meaning 'Ruler of the Romans', reflects the spirit of female leadership and power that resonated in spiritual and secular realms, inspiring those who sought to defy the constraints of societal expectations. Today, the name Zenobia encourages those who aspire to leadership roles and ambitious pursuits, not just in the worldly sense but also in the context of their spiritual development.
